svg.title: The reliability diagram: 10 trivia predictions, over-confident vs. well-calibrated
svg.desc: Ten confidence values (0.6, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.8, 0.9, 0.9, 0.9, 1.0, 1.0) grouped into three bins, [0.6, 0.8) with n=3, [0.8, 1.0) with n=5, and [1.0] with n=2, plotted as mean confidence versus accuracy against a dashed diagonal where confidence equals accuracy. The over-confident model's points sit below the diagonal at (0.633, 0.333), (0.860, 0.400), and (1.000, 0.500), giving gaps of 0.300, 0.460, and 0.500; its overall mean confidence is 0.82 against an actual accuracy of 0.40. The well-calibrated model uses the same confidences but its points sit near the diagonal at (0.633, 0.667), (0.860, 0.800), and (1.000, 1.000), giving gaps of 0.033, 0.060, and 0.000; its overall accuracy is 0.80. Weighting each bin's gap by its share of the 10 predictions gives an expected calibration error, ECE, of 0.420 for the over-confident model and 0.040 for the well-calibrated model, a 10.5 times shrink. The Brier score, the mean squared error between confidence and outcome, falls from 0.432 to 0.172 over the same pair.
